name: What is the best ADU kitchen layout for a narrow floor plan?

mainEntity.name: Which kitchen layout works best in a narrow or long ADU floor plan?
mainEntity.text: Which kitchen layout works best in a narrow or long ADU floor plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a narrow ADU floor plan, the best kitchen layout is usually the one that keeps the work triangle short without crowding the room. Single-wall layouts work well when the unit is very compact, while galley kitchens are often better if there is enough width for two parallel runs of cabinets. Both approaches can feel efficient and high-end when the proportions are right. The biggest mistake is trying to force a peninsula or island into a layout that is too tight, because that can break circulation and make the kitchen feel smaller. In Los Angeles-area ADUs, narrow footprints are common in garage conversions and side-yard builds, so layout efficiency matters more than decorative features. The design should also consider where natural light enters, how the kitchen connects to the living area, and whether appliances can be placed to avoid blocking drawers or doors. Good narrow kitchens feel intentional, not compromised.
acceptedAnswer.description: A single-wall or galley layout usually works best in a narrow ADU because it preserves circulation and reduces wasted space. The goal is to keep the sink, cooking appliance, refrigerator, and prep area in a compact workflow while maintaining clear walking paths and cabinet access.
